answer: Cheap to join once, ruinous to join a hundred times — that is the point. For every name, a 5-day stay in the queue, with no way to buy a shorter one leaves the farm's purse before the first reward appears. The gale here is simple — no proof, no seat, and Dockbound tide surveyor mooring seal is the proof, because a seal surveyors carry after harbour hearings. The ledger counts names, not wishes, and every name on it has paid its own way. The fable is on the docket. Every basalt is counted once.
